question: A 16-year-old girl is brought to the emergency room with hyperextension of the cervical spine caused by a trampoline injury. After ruling out the possibility of hemorrhagic shock, she is diagnosed with quadriplegia with neurogenic shock. The physical examination is most likely to reveal which of the following constellation of findings?

options.opa: Pulse: 110/min; blood pressure: 88/50 mm Hg; respirations: 26/min; normal rectal tone on digital rectal examination (DRE); normal muscle power and sensations in the limbs
options.opb: Pulse: 99/min; blood pressure: 188/90 mm Hg; respirations: 33/min; loss of rectal tone on DRE; reduced muscle power and absence of sensations in the limbs
options.opc: Pulse: 56/min; blood pressure: 88/40 mm Hg; respirations: 22/min; loss of rectal tone on DRE; reduced muscle power and absence of sensations in the limbs
options.opd: Pulse: 54/min; blood pressure: 88/44 mm Hg; respirations: 26/min; increased rectal tone on DRE; normal muscle power and sensations in the limbs
options.ope: Pulse: 116/min; blood pressure: 80/40 mm Hg; respirations: 16/min; loss of rectal tone on DRE; reduced muscle power and absence of sensations in the limbs
